LanguageData.YaOpt.Message.ButterCompatibilityNotEnab: You have both YaOpt and Butter++ installed. The compatibility mode of Butter++ must be enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Message.ButterCompatibilityForceEn: You have both YaOpt and Butter++ installed. The compatibility mode of Butter++ was enforced.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Message.PerformanceOptimizerGetCom: You have both YaOpt and Performance Optimizer installed, and the multi-threaded optimizations of YaOpt is enabled. If you encounter the "System.InvalidOperationException: Collection was modified" error randomly but infrequently in the game, try disable "Faster GetComp methods replacement" of Performance Optimizer.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Message.PerformanceFishSeeConsole: You have both YaOpt and Performance Fish installed, and you have enabled the options that have compatibility issues. See the console for details.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Message.ErrorWhilePatching: YaOpt encountered an error while applying settings. The game may not function correctly. Check the console for details.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Message.RequireReload: Changed settings will take effect after loading a save or restarting the game.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DebugOutput.Desc: Output debug info to the console. Enabling this may slightly reduce game speed, as the game records the entire stack trace for each console message, which is an expensive operation.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MaterialGetColor.De: Caches material colors to reduce the overhead of frequent calls to the underlying engine function. The cache is automatically updated when the material color changes.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ColoredText.Desc: Optimizes the parsing performance of rich text (e.g., colored text). The vanilla game uses a slow overload of IndexOf (involving culture-sensitive checks) to locate tags. This optimization replaces it with a faster overload that performs a direct ordinal comparison.
Starts the render preparation for dynamic objects earlier. While vanilla supports parallel preparation, it starts after the static terrain is drawn. This optimization dispatches the preparation jobs before drawing the terrain, allowing worker threads to process object data concurrently with the main thread's terrain rendering, effectively hiding the latency.
Strict adherence to rendering standards required: any mod rendering during the preparation phase (which violates vanilla standards) will result in objects being occluded by the terrain.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PrepareBatchCount.D: The vanilla game uses a large batch size for parallel render preparation. However, rendering costs vary greatly between objects (e.g., pawns vs. items), and objects are often clustered (e.g., raids). This leads to thread imbalance where some threads finish early while others struggle with heavy batches. This optimization reduces the batch size, allowing the work-stealing algorithm to distribute the load more evenly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelMaterialUpd: Moves material parameter updates to the parallel rendering preparation phase. Vanilla performs these on the main thread, even though they usually don't require it. If a mod overrides material updates for specific objects (which might be unsafe), this optimization will automatically fall back to the main thread for those objects.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastRecacheRequeste: Optimizes the check for whether an object needs to regenerate render parameters. Vanilla checks this by recursively calling every child node in the render tree. Since 97% of render trees are shallow (less than or equal to 4 layers), this optimization inlines the check for the first 4 layers into a single function, avoiding virtual function call overhead. Note: Performance profiler shows only a minor improvement. This optimization may be removed in future versions.
Assumes all render nodes use the vanilla cache update check logic. If a mod overrides the cache update check mechanism (detected at startup), this optimization is automatically disabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Des: Vanilla loads all mod textures into VRAM at startup. This optimization loads textures only when they are first requested, reducing startup time and VRAM usage, but causing stutters when textures are loaded in-game. Note that texture unloading is not yet implemented, so VRAM usage may eventually reach peak levels during long play sessions.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Com: This can cause inaccurate statistics in Graphics Settings+ and ImageOpt.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Pre: Due to Harmony limitation in patching generic methods, this is implemented via prepatch. It requires Prepatcher Mod. If you switch this option, you need to restart the game for this optimization to take effect.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Dds: Only enable lazy loading for DDS textures (and Zstd compressed DDS from ImageOpt). Non-DDS formats require extra time to convert to a renderable format upon loading, causing noticeable stuttering during runtime loading.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Rad: Basic optimization only delays the loading of textures for pawns and items. Due to vanilla code, building textures are always loaded at game startup to generate texture atlases and serve as preview icons. Enabling this option will downsample textures larger than 256 pixels to 256 pixels at game startup, loading the full texture only when actually used in the game. Because loading detection is required when creating things, it slightly increases the overhead of thing creation, resulting in a slight increase in stuttering during game loading and when a large number of objects are created on the map. It is recommended to enable this option only if VRAM usage is still tight after enabling basic optimization. Furthermore, this option only supports DDS (and Zstd compressed DDS) textures.
Optimizes XML patch operations by simplifying common XPath expressions. If an XPath expression matches a simple pattern like "Defs/DefType[defName='DefName']", this optimization bypasses the complex XPath engine and uses a faster direct node lookup. This speeds up the game startup process.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastTranslationInje: Optimizes the process of injecting translation text into XML data at startup. The game checks for errors such as duplicate field injections. The vanilla implementation performs this check with O(N^2) complexity. This optimization replaces the linear search with a hash table lookup, reducing the complexity to O(N). This speeds up game startup, especially for non-English languages.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RuntimeInfoCache.De: Caches type information at startup to accelerate Harmony type retrieval. This speeds up Harmony patch processing for some mods, improving game startup time in modded environments. It has no effect in a vanilla environment.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FixTextureAtlas.Des: Fixes a vanilla bug where texture atlases smaller than 512x512 have Mipmaps enabled but not populated, causing visual corruption (colored stripes) when zooming out. This issue typically affects scatterable items (e.g. pebbles) from high-res texture mods. It occurs in specific mod combinations where the atlas size falls into the problematic range.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MapMeshUpdateThrott: Throttles the update frequency of the map mesh (terrain rendering). In vanilla, any change in snow or dust thickness triggers an immediate mesh update in the rendering frame, consuming significant resources during frequent changes (e.g., snowfall or melting). This optimization imposes a minimum real-time interval between updates. The map is forcibly updated when the game is paused.

Adjusts the minimum real-time interval between two updates. Note that since the game uses incremental updates for terrain, this option has diminishing returns. Setting the interval to 1000ms won't reduce update overhead to 1/10th of 100ms, because the number of cells to process per update increases. Recommended values are 300 or 500. If you don't care about visual lag, 1000 is also acceptable.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PRNRWorker: Pawn Render Node Worker Cache Fix
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PRNRWorker.Desc: The initialization of PawnRenderNodeProperties.Worker is slow. The game has a built-in cache for it. However, due to a coding oversight, the cache will never be read. This optimization fixes the bug to correctly use the cache.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GraphicTextureCache: Caches the textures required for Graphic_Multi initialization. Vanilla constructs texture paths for all four cardinal directions using string concatenation and performs asset lookups every time. This optimization caches the resolved textures, eliminating these redundant operations. Originally designed for Humanoid Alien Races, but benefits any mod that frequently rebuilds graphics. Note: This optimization may cause texture hot reload in developer options to fail.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.Silhouette.Desc: Optimizes the lookup performance of the silhouette (off-screen icon) cache by implementing a better comparison mechanism.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ToggleTabCheck.Desc: Throttles the visibility check for toggleable tabs (e.g. the Mechanoid tab). Some modded tabs perform complex, uncached queries every frame to decide if they should be hidden. This optimization limits these checks to once every 500ms. Visibility is forcibly refreshed when pausing, unpausing, or switching maps.
Accelerates the matrix computation step in render preparation using Burst. Vanilla intended to use Burst for this heavy calculation but failed due to a coding oversight. This optimization implements a working Burst solution.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingGetComp.Desc: Vanilla GetComp is fast when finding an existing component but very slow when looking for a missing one. Unfortunately, the only way to check if a component exists is to query it and wait for a failure. This optimization rewrites the lookup mechanism to ensure fast failure when searching for non-existent components.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingGetComp.Prepat: Due to Harmony limitation in patching generic methods, this is implemented via prepatch. It requires Prepatcher Mod. If you switch this option, you need to restart the game for this optimization to take effect.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.De: Introduces limited multithreading for pawn updates. Multithreading handles pawn job interruption checks, constant job checks, and mood updates.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.St: If the error log shows "ParallelPawnTickManager" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Co: Mods must not produce side effects (e.g., altering game time or state) inside job failure condition checks. Failure conditions might be evaluated twice per frame (once in the predictor, once in the main thread).
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Mu: Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Jo: Predicts whether a pawn's current job will fail or be interrupted (e.g., by enemies) in the current frame. If the prediction passes, the check on the main thread is skipped; otherwise, the main thread re-runs the standard check to ensure correctness.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Co: Predict whether a constant job will be executed in the current frame. A constant job refers to a high-priority action, such as evading enemies or searching for oxygen in space.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelJobGiver.De: Job issuance is one of the most performance-intensive operations in the game. It normally iterates through a prioritized list of allowed jobs until a valid one is found. This optimization uses multi-threading to check this list. When a thread finds a valid job, it truncates the search sequence at that point (discarding lower-priority jobs), waits for other threads checking higher-priority jobs to complete, and then issues the highest-priority valid job found.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelJobGiver.St: If the error log shows "ParallelJobGiver" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelJobGiver.Co: Mods must not produce side effects (e.g., altering game state) during job issuance checks and must not perform non-thread-safe operations. Mods should never assume that a generated job will definitely be executed (multiple valid jobs may be generated in parallel, but only the highest-priority one is adopted; others are discarded).
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelJobGiver.Mu: Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPostMapTick: Executes map steady environment effects, water freezing and gas diffusion updates using multi-threading.
If the error log shows "SteadyEnvironmentEffects", "TempTerrainManager", or "GasGrid" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelThoughtUpda: Executes pawn thought updates using multi-threading.

If the error log shows "ParallelThoughtRecalculatingJob", "ParallelThoughtCreatingJob", "ParallelPreceptThoughtCreatingJob", "ParallelThoughtAddingJob", or "ParallelThoughtUpdater" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdeoCheck.Desc: Optimizes the check for whether an Ideoligion allows a specific action. Vanilla iterates through all precepts to make this determination. This optimization creates a cache of precepts that impose restrictions whenever precepts are updated. When checking permissions, it only iterates through these cached restrictive precepts, ignoring irrelevant ones.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdleThrottle.Desc:
Throttles the interruption idle check for idle pawns (sleeping and wandering) in the game. This optimization include three parts, the latter two of which are configurable:
1. Optimize the bed availability check for lying pawns. The vanilla game checks the availability of the current bed for lying pawns every tick, which is necessary but involves some heavy calculations, such as determining whether a sick pawns has recovered. After throttling, a full check will be performed every 15 ticks (0.25 seconds), and the other 14 ticks will only perform simple, quick and necessary checks, such as determining whether the bed is destroyed.
2. Optimize the check interval for lying pawns waking up to work. In the vanilla game, lying pawns would perform a work check every 211 ticks. This optimization can extend this interval and also make the interval dynamic, controlling it based on the number of lying colonists, ensuring that pawns in small colonies can still respond quickly to emergencies.
3. Optimize the work check interval for idle pawns. In the vanilla game, idle colonists would perform a work check on every 125~200 ticks. This optimization can extend this interval and also make it dynamic, controlling the interval based on the number of colonists with nothing to do.
Adjusts the check interval for lying pawns to get up and work, in ticks. The vanilla is 211 ticks.
Controls the check interval for lying pawns to get up and work based on the number of lying colonists.
Check interval when the number of colonists lying in bed is less than or equal to the minimum number, in ticks, the vanilla is 211 ticks.

The check interval when the number of colonists lying in bed is greater than or equal to the maximum number, in ticks. When the number of lying colonists is between the minimum and maximum number, the interval is calculated using linear interpolation.
The check interval will be minimized when the number of colonists in bed is less than or equal to this number.

When the number of colonists in bed is greater than or equal to this number, the check interval will reach its maximum. When the number is between the minimum and maximum number, the check interval will increase linearly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdleThrottle.StopWa: Adjusts the check interval for idle pawns to find work, in ticks. The vanilla is at least 125 ticks.\nThe actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.\nThe random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1}

Dynamic interval Controls the check interval for idle colonists looking for work based on the number of idle colonists. Minest Interval: {0} Adjusts the check interval when the number of idle colonists is less than or equal to the minimum number, in ticks. The vanilla is at least 125 ticks.
The actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.
The random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1} Maximum Interval: {0} Adjusts the check interval when the number of idle colonists is greater than or equal to the maximum number, in ticks. When the number of idle colonists is between the minimum and maximum number, the interval is calculated using linear interpolation.
The actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.
The random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1} Minimum number of people: {0} The check interval will be minimized when the number of idle colonists is less than or equal to this number. Maximum Number of People: {0} When the number of idle colonists is greater than or equal to this number, the check interval will reach its maximum. When the number is between the minimum and maximum number, the check interval will increase linearly. Plant Sway Optimization Vanilla updates wind strength parameters for all plant materials every logic tick, which is unnecessary. This optimization restricts these updates to render frames only. Fast Thing Removal Optimizes the efficiency of removing objects from the game. Vanilla searches through lists linearly to remove objects. This optimization tracks object positions using indices, allowing for direct removal by swapping the removed object with the last one in the list. Update Rate Calculation Optimization The game calculates the visibility of things on the screen every tick and reduces the update rate of off-screen things. However, this calculation is a bit complicated, incurring some overhead. This optimization fine-tunes the visibility check, slightly relaxing the criteria and reducing the overhead of update rate calculation. The trade-off is that under certain conditions, a few things close to the screen edge but invisible may be mistakenly identified as visible, causing the system to increase their update rate and resulting in runtime overhead. However, in most cases, this optimization is worthwhile. Map Pawn Retrieval Optimization Optimizes the code for retrieving pawns on the map in the game, eliminating some redundant calculations. In addition, it also reduces the workload of determining childcare. In vanilla game, when searching for hungry babies, it would search not only those already on the map but also containers, a step that accounted for a large portion of the computation. Therefore, this optimization only performs a full map container search every three checks, and the other two checks only examine babies outside of containers. Also optimizes character retrieval in the colonist portrait bar. If you have installed a portrait bar mod and find its functionality is not working, you can try disabling this optimization. Target Finding Optimization Optimizes target finding calculations during combat, eliminating some redundant calculations. Thing Holder Retrieval Optimization Optimizes recursive search of thing containers, reducing the overhead of checking non-container contents. Meditation Tick Throttling Throttles the meditation update frequency from every tick to once every 100 ticks (with 100x effect compensation). Meditation is surprisingly expensive, especially for tribal psycasters scanning for Anima grass every frame. Note: This slightly impacts gameplay, as partial progress (avg. 50 ticks / 0.83s) is lost when meditation is interrupted. Tested and compatible with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded. May conflict with other mods that heavily alter meditation mechanics. This feature overlaps with Performance Esmolas, and will using its optimization implementation if it's present. Extended Stat Caching Extends the vanilla stat caching system to include Comfortable Temperature and Filth Rate. Comfortable Temperature is updated every 20 ticks (and forcibly refreshed when apparel changes), while Filth Rate is updated every 60 ticks. This reduces the overhead of frequently accessing these expensive stats. All FPS TPS Misc
